title: Month 33
subtitle: The three-year visit is next month. It is the last one in this guide.

baby.development: Your child speaks in sentences, can jump, pedal, and climb. They can follow a three-step instruction and are starting to understand the idea of yesterday and tomorrow.

you.body: If you are pregnant again, the three-year gap is the one where the older child can understand that a baby is coming. Tell them early and simply.
you.mind: Thirty-three months is when the child starts to ask about the baby, or about the world, in a way that has an answer. Answer it.

coreActions.title: Book the three-year visit
coreActions.why: This is the last visit in this guide, and it is the one where preschool readiness and language get checked.
coreActions.detail: The three-year visit usually has no vaccines if the eighteen-month set is complete. The doctor will check language, movement, teeth, and growth, and will ask about preschool and toilet learning. Bring the questions.

coreActions.title: Teach yesterday, today, and tomorrow
coreActions.why: Time words are abstract and they are learned from hearing them used about real events.
coreActions.detail: Yesterday we went to the park. Tomorrow we will see grandma. Use a calendar on the wall and point at the day. A child who understands yesterday and tomorrow at three is on track.

coreActions.title: Name feelings out loud, including your own
coreActions.why: A child who has words for a feeling has something to do with it other than hit.
coreActions.detail: I am frustrated because the traffic is slow. You are disappointed that the park is closed. Name it, do not fix it. A feelings chart on the wall helps. This is the foundation for the conversations at four and five.

alsoKnow.title: Sentences of three or more words
alsoKnow.body: Most three-year-olds speak in sentences of three or more words and can be understood by strangers most of the time. A child who is not understood at three is worth raising at the visit.

alsoKnow.title: An hour a day, and not alone
alsoKnow.body: The recommendation for two to five is no more than an hour a day of high-quality content, watched with an adult. A screen alone in a room is the thing to avoid.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
A fall from a height, or a head injury with vomiting or unusual sleepiness
